title: For patients
summary: Your own log: logging, red flags, your care team, and your account.
body:
LipNode is a daily log for lipedema: surgery recovery and the long haul. These are the questions patients ask most. If yours is not here, there is a Contact us form at the bottom of the You screen.

GETTING STARTED:

What is LipNode?

A daily logbook for your own body. You record what goes in, what comes out, how you feel, what you measure, and what you want to ask your surgeon. The app totals it up, watches for a short list of warning signs, and turns any stretch of days into a PDF you can hand over at an appointment.

Is this my medical record?

No. Nothing you write here reaches your surgeon, your clinic, or your chart. Your surgeon sees it only if you show them or hand them the PDF. It is your own record of your own days.

Do I need to have had surgery to use it?

No. Start a maintenance log instead and your days run by calendar date with no surgery day to count from. You can add a surgery later and keep the maintenance log alongside it.

What is day zero?

The date of your surgery. Once you have entered it, every day is labelled by its distance from that date, so "Post-op day 9" reads the same to you and to your surgeon. A maintenance log has no day zero and uses the calendar date.

Can I track two surgeries at once?

Yes. Each keeps its own days, its own trackers and its own goals. The chip row at the top of Today, Day by Day and Trends switches between them, or shows all of them on one timeline.

LOGGING YOUR DAYS:

How do I log something?

Open Today and tap a tile. Each tile opens one short form. The check-in is the wide button at the top: it asks one measure per screen, so a rough morning is still a handful of taps.

Can I change which tiles I see, and their order?

Yes. Setup, then What to track, turns each tracker on or off for that surgery. To reorder the tiles, tap Edit next to "Log an entry" on Today, or press and hold any tile, then drag.

Can I log something for a day I missed?

Yes. Use the arrows either side of the date on a day page to step back, or Jump to a day on Day by Day to open any date. A day you never touched opens just the same, so a day missed while you were unwell can still be filled in afterwards.

Can I fix or delete an entry?

Tap the entry on the day's timeline. The form reopens with what you saved. Delete is below Save and asks before it removes anything, because deleting cannot be undone.

What happens to what I already logged if I turn a tracker off?

Nothing. It hides the tile and stops it appearing on the day card. Everything already recorded stays, and comes back if you turn the tracker on again.

Why does the check-in ask at set times?

Because a score only means something next to another score taken at the same point in the day. Setup, then Check-in, is where you name the times. The form picks whichever one has most recently passed.

What are goals for?

A goal turns a number into a fraction. "46 oz" tells you less than "46 of 64 oz", so a tracker with a goal gets a bar on Day totals and a line on Trends. Leave one blank and that tracker just reports the number.

Did my entry save?

The app tells you either way. A save that worked says so briefly. A save that failed says what went wrong and offers Retry, and what you typed stays on the screen until it lands.

RED FLAGS:

What is the red flag check?

Twelve things that most often mean call someone after this surgery. Your surgeons gave the list. You answer them once a day, and your answers, the time, whether you called and what you did all go into the PDF.

Why is a question already answered when I open it?

Because something you logged that day looks like a yes. It is marked with a sparkle and a line saying which entry it came from. It is a suggestion, not a verdict: tap either answer to override it. The app only ever suggests yes, so it can never talk you out of a flag you would have raised.

What should I do if I answer yes?

Call. Every one of those twelve is on the list because your surgeon wants to hear about it, and the card carries a button that dials the number on your record. If you cannot breathe, have chest pain, are confused or cannot be woken, call emergency services instead and do not wait for the office.

Does the app call anyone for me?

No. It never contacts your surgeon, your clinic, or emergency services. It records what you decided and makes the number easy to reach.

What fever number does it use?

Whatever you entered in "Call if fever over" on your surgery or maintenance log. Leave it blank and the app uses 101.5 F, which is the line most surgeons give but is not yours until you enter yours. The question on the card names whichever number is in force, so you always know what you are answering against.

If I change an answer later, what happens to the old one?

The new answer replaces it. Answers save as you tap them, and only the newest one is kept, so if something changes during the day, answer again.

YOUR CARE TEAM:

Who can see my log?

You, and only the people you add yourself. Nobody else.

How do I add someone?

Care, then Care team, then the plus button. Enter their email and name. They get an invitation email and you get a six-character code. Your own date of birth has to be on your account first, because it is the second thing they need.

What does someone need to open my log?

Two things: the six-character code, and your date of birth. Neither one works without the other.

Why does the email not carry either one?

Because the email alone would be enough. Having their address is what identifies them; the code and your date of birth are what let them in. If any of it travelled in the same message, one mistyped address would hand over everything. Read the code out, text it, or write it down, and tell them your date of birth the same way.

Where do I find the code again?

Care, then Care team. Anyone who has not opened the log yet shows their code on their row, so you do not have to go looking. Tap the row to send the invitation email again.

What can a care team member do?

Read. All of it: every entry, every day, every red flag, your measurements and your photos. They cannot add, edit or delete anything, and they cannot add anyone else.

Can I give someone permission to write?

Not today. Every care team member is read only.

How do I remove someone?

Care, then Care team, tap their row, then Remove. Their access ends immediately. You can add them again later, which issues a new code.

They say it is not working.

Case and the dash in the code do not matter, so 7k2qm4 and 7K2-QM4 are the same. Check the date of birth too: the app does not say which of the two was wrong, on purpose, because saying so would turn two checks into one. If it still fails, remove them and add them again.

SHARING AND EXPORT:

How do I show my surgeon?

Setup, then Download a PDF. Pick a day or a range and it builds on your phone. It carries the surgery details, your goals, the care team, garments, med groups, trends, red flags and your questions.

Where does the PDF go?

Wherever you send it. Once it leaves the app it is an ordinary file, and the app has no say in where it ends up.

YOUR ACCOUNT:

Can I use this on more than one device?

Yes. Your log lives on your account, so signing in anywhere shows the same days. Appearance, text size and the tile order are per device.

Can I install it like an app?

On iPhone: open it in Safari, tap the Share button, then Add to Home Screen. It then opens full screen with no browser bar. Safari never offers this by itself, so you have to go and get it.

Can I make the text bigger?

Yes. You, then Appearance, then Text size. It changes the whole app on that device straight away.

Does it work without signal?

Not yet. Entries save to your account as you make them, so a drop-out can stop one landing. The app tells you when that happens and keeps what you typed, so nothing is lost silently.

How do I delete everything?

You, then Delete my account. It asks you to type your email address, then removes your login and the whole log: every entry, every day, every surgery, your measurements, garments, med groups and your care team's access. Permanent, with no undo.

title: For care team members
summary: Reading someone else's log: getting in, what you can do, and how to step away.
body:
Someone has trusted you with their medical log. These are the questions care team members ask most. If yours is not here, there is a Contact us form at the bottom of the You screen.

GETTING IN:

Someone added me. What do I do?

Create an account with the email address they used, sign in, and enter the six-character code they read out to you along with their date of birth. That opens their log.

Why do I need a code and their date of birth?

The email tells you the log exists. The code proves the patient meant you. Their date of birth proves you are the person she meant to read it to. The invitation email carries neither, so an invitation that reaches the wrong inbox opens nothing.

Where do I get them?

From the patient, out loud or by text. Not from the app, not from the email, and nobody else can look them up for you.

It is not working.

Case and the dash in the code do not matter. Check the date of birth as well: the app will not say which of the two was wrong, because saying so would turn two checks into one. If it still fails, ask them to check the code on their Care screen.

I signed in and it says I am not on a log.

Nobody has added you yet, or they used a different email address. Only the patient can add you. Ask them to add the exact address you signed in with.

Can I be on more than one person's care team?

Yes. You, then Logs you help with, lists every one you have opened. One is open at a time, and the top of the screen always names whose log you are reading.

WHAT YOU CAN DO:

What can I see?

Everything in that patient's log: every entry, the timeline, day totals, the red flag check and what they wrote about it, their questions for the surgeon, their measurements, and any photos they attached.

Can I add or change anything?

No. Every care team member is read only. You cannot log an entry, answer a red flag, or edit anything the patient wrote.

Can I log on their behalf while they are asleep?

Not in the app. Write it down and have them enter it, or have them hand you their own signed-in phone.

Can I export the PDF?

Yes, from Setup, for the log you have open. Treat it as their health information: it is theirs, not yours, and where it goes after you export it is on you.

READING A LOG WELL:

Where should I start?

Today, then Day totals, then the red flag check. Totals say whether the day went the way it should. The red flag check says whether anything needs a phone call.

What do the two flag shapes mean?

On Day totals, a swallowtail flag was raised by the patient's own entries. A straight pennant was raised by the patient answering the question herself. Both count, and there is a key under the row.

What does "Post-op day 9" mean?

Nine days since the surgery date on that record. A maintenance log has no surgery date and shows the calendar date instead.

Their log looks worrying. What do I do?

Talk to them, and get them to call their surgeon's office. The number is on the surgery record in Setup, and the red flag card has a button that dials it. If it looks like an emergency, call emergency services. The app notifies nobody: if you saw it, you are the notification.

YOUR ACCOUNT:

Am I in their log as a person?

Yes. Your name and email are on their care team list, along with whether you have opened it. They can remove you at any time, which ends your access immediately.

How do I step away?

You, then Logs you help with, then Leave this care team. That ends your access to that log. It does not touch anything the patient recorded, and they can add you again later.

What happens if I delete my account?

Your login goes, and you come off every care team you are on. The patients' logs are untouched.
